threads.hunk:
@@ -4,6 +4,14 @@
 
 ### ⚠️ Breaking changes
 
+- Couchbase 2.x SQL queries now use the shared SQL attribute extractor and no longer emit
+  `db.operation.name`. SQL query attributes and span names are derived from the raw query text.
+  Disabling query sanitization now affects only `db.query.text`: `db.query.summary` and
+  query-derived span names are still produced, matching other SQL instrumentations. This applies
+  to both `otel.instrumentation.couchbase.query-sanitization.enabled=false` and declarative
+  `java.couchbase.query_sanitization.enabled: false`, including when inherited from the common
+  database setting. Non-query operations, Couchbase view queries, and existing configuration names
+  and precedence are unchanged.

threads.body: [Testing] The new sanitization coverage constructs `SqlClientAttributesExtractor` directly, so it never exercises this `DbConfig` lookup or the singleton/instrumenter selection used by an installed agent. A regression in the Couchbase flat, declarative, or inherited common setting could therefore leave `db.query.text` masked while these tests still pass. Please add agent-backed coverage that disables sanitization through the real configuration path and asserts raw `db.query.text` while the query summary and span name remain derived.

replies.body:
Addressed in df0172ff82be3eff2d9a960129377e8da3a4fefa.

Added installed-agent coverage invoking the real CouchbaseAsyncBucket.query path with an N1qlQuery and a stub transport. Separate JVMs cover default sanitization, Couchbase flat and declarative disablement, and inherited common flat and declarative disablement. The Couchbase declarative fixture overrides an enabled common setting. Exact exported attributes assert raw or masked db.query.text as configured and unchanged derived db.query.summary and span name. All five cases and the experimental variant passed.

threads.body: @copilot Please address the remaining [metadata collection feedback](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20478#discussion_r4238000346). The sanitization-disabled task remains in `instrumentations.sh`. InfluxDB and OpenSearch have similar tasks and metadata labels, but neither task is enrolled in that collection list. This regression-only variant should stay in `check`, leave the collection list, drop `metadataConfig`, and explicitly set `collectMetadata=false`.

replies.body: Addressed in commit `COMMIT_PENDING`: the disabled variant remains in `check`, is removed from metadata collection, and now sets `collectMetadata=false` without `metadataConfig`.
